profile.summary: DUD-E is a virtual screening benchmark: for each of 102 protein targets it supplies a set of known active compounds and, for every active, 50 decoy molecules chosen to match it on physico-chemical properties while being topologically dissimilar. A docking program or scoring model ranks the pooled library for a target, and the benchmark measures how far the actives rise above the decoys, reported as an adjusted logarithmic area under the ROC curve and an enrichment factor at 1 per cent. The actives come from ChEMBL09, or the literature for AmpC beta-lactamase, with affinities of 1 micromolar or better, molecular weight under 600 and fewer than 20 rotatable bonds, clustered to 22,886 ligands, and the decoys from ZINC. It is used to compare docking programs and scoring functions, and a later study shows that machine learning models trained on it can score well without learning anything about binding.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Ligand enrichment: whether a method puts known binders near the top of a library that is otherwise full of molecules that look like them but are not known to bind. The decoys are the point. They are matched to each active on six physico-chemical properties, so a method cannot win by preferring heavy or greasy molecules, and they are topologically dissimilar to the actives, so the task is not fingerprint matching. The target list was chosen for diversity, adding classes such as G protein coupled receptors and ion channels that the original DUD lacked. What the benchmark does not measure, as the authors of a later study showed, is whether a model has learned protein-ligand interaction physics.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Actives come from ChEMBL09: compounds assigned to a protein target with a confidence score of at least 4 and an affinity of 1 micromolar or better. Raw ligands also had to have a molecular weight under 600 and fewer than 20 rotatable bonds, which gives 66,695 raw ligands. For AmpC beta-lactamase the ChEMBL09 ligands are covalent, so its ligands were compiled by hand from the literature instead. Molecules with no measurable affinity at 30 micromolar or worse are kept as experimental decoys, and the in-between cases are kept separately as marginal. Each target's ligands are clustered to leave 22,886 clustered ligands for chemotype diversity. Targets are defined by UniProt gene prefix with species pooled, and each target gets one X-ray structure, chosen by an automated docking campaign over thousands of PDB entries with preference for resolution, enrichment and the human orthologue, with manual intervention where the automated preparation failed. Decoys are drawn from ZINC: for each unique set of six properties of a protonated ligand, molecular weight, estimated log P, rotatable bonds, hydrogen bond acceptors and donors and net charge, a pool of a few thousand candidates is gathered by widening or narrowing property windows in seven steps, ECFP4 fingerprints are computed, the pool is sorted by maximum Tanimoto similarity to any ligand, the most dissimilar quarter is kept, duplicates are spread evenly over the ligands, and 50 decoys are picked at random. That gives 1,411,214 computational decoys in all.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: A method ranks the library for one target, actives and decoys together, and the ranking is scored. The paper's primary measure is the adjusted LogAUC at 0.001, which is the area under the ROC curve on a semi-logarithmic x-axis spanning three decades, with the random curve's 14.462 per cent subtracted so that random performance is 0 per cent and higher is better. The ROC-based enrichment factor at 1 per cent is also reported: the percentage of ligands found by the point where 1 per cent of the decoys have been found, which the authors prefer to a traditional enrichment factor. Plain ROC AUC is noted as a common alternative. The authors' own numbers come from docking with DOCK 3.6 using solvent-excluded volume ligand desolvation, with conformations from Omega, and they report per-target LogAUC and enrichment factor values in their target table. Scores are per target; the benchmark defines no single aggregate.

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: The data are downloaded from the benchmark's own site, either target by target, by subset such as the G protein coupled receptor or kinase groups, or as one package, and the site says the files can also be browsed directly under its db directory without JavaScript. Each target ships the chosen receptor structure and the active and decoy sets, in mol2 and SDF formats. There is no scoring server: a user docks or scores the molecules with their own program and computes the enrichment metrics themselves. The site also runs a decoy generation service, so the same protocol can be applied to a user's own ligand list for a target that is not in the set.

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: None. DUD-E is a test set, not a train and test division: each target is an independent screening problem with its own actives and decoys, and the authors say targets are independent of one another so that they can be added, deleted or replaced. Methods that train on DUD-E, as machine learning work does, have to invent their own split, and Chen et al. show that the usual choice, separating targets by sequence similarity, rests on an untested assumption about their actives.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Online Tools section; Chen et al. 2019: Methods and Discussion

quotes.text: Targets are independent of one another, both in ligands and decoys, allowing target addition, deletion, or replacement.
Training and test subsets of the DUD-E dataset were constructed in several different ways.

To test a model’s capacity for generalization, many groups have used sequence similarity filters to separate DUD-E targets into diverse training and testing sets. However, this is based on the untested assumption that targets in DUD-E with low sequence similarity have distinct actives.

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: Adjusted LogAUC at 0.001, higher is better: the ROC area in semi-logarithmic space over three decades, with the random curve's 14.462 per cent subtracted so random is 0. Alongside it the ROC-based enrichment factor at 1 per cent, higher is better, the percentage of ligands recovered when 1 per cent of the decoys have been recovered. Plain ROC AUC is named as a common metric and is what later machine learning work reports.

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: Within a target, two. Ligands are clustered by Bemis-Murcko frameworks so that near-identical analogues do not dominate, and decoys are filtered to be topologically dissimilar to the actives, keeping only the most dissimilar quarter of the candidate pool by ECFP4 Tanimoto similarity. There is no control across targets, and no control for a model trained on DUD-E: Chen et al. report that models can separate actives from decoys from the ligand alone, with no receptor, which they attribute to analogue bias among each target's actives and to the way the decoys were chosen.

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: No replicates or intervals are defined by the benchmark: a target's score is a single ranking of a fixed library. The authors do provide a way to probe one source of variance, since the final decoy pick is random where possible, so several decoy sets can be generated for the same ligands to test whether a method is overfitted to the canonical decoys.

notes: DUD-E is a released suite with no leaderboard and no scoring code: results are computed by whoever runs it, so results_url points to the project site rather than to a results table. The decoy count 1,411,214 is the total number of computational decoys across all 102 targets, and 9,219 is the number of experimentally measured decoys; 22,886 is the clustered active count, out of 66,695 raw ligands. Numbers quoted from the paper's characteristics table include the surrounding XML cell markup, because each cell is a separate element. No data licence is printed: the project page says the set is free to use and carries a UC Regents copyright line, and the paper is under ACS AuthorChoice terms, so no licence identifier is recorded for either. The project page announces a newer set, DUDE-Z, at dudez.docking.org, which was not fetched. The site's download path used in the run guide is taken from the page's own full-package link text and may have changed; the page states the files can be browsed under /db/. The page also carries a correspondence address, which is not reproduced here.
